events.title: The Battle of the Milvian Bridge
events.shortBlurb: Constantine conquered under the sign of the Cross, opening the way to the toleration of Christianity…
body: On 28 October 312 the army of Constantine met that of his rival Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge, where the Via Flaminia crossed the Tiber north of Rome. Maxentius held the city; Constantine had marched the length of Italy to wrest it from him.

Christian writers near the event tell of a sign given before the battle. Lactantius records that Constantine was warned in a dream to mark the heavenly sign of God, the Chi-Rho monogram of Christ, on his soldiers' shields; Eusebius, writing from the emperor's own account, tells of a cross of light above the midday sun with the words "In this, conquer" — in Latin, in hoc signo vinces.

Maxentius drowned in the Tiber when the bridge of boats behind him collapsed under his fleeing army. Constantine entered Rome master of the West, and the following year, 313, agreed with his colleague Licinius at Milan upon full liberty of worship for Christians. The long age of persecution was closing, and the Church emerged from the catacombs into public life.

events.title: The election of Pope John XXIII
events.shortBlurb: The cardinals chose the aged Angelo Roncalli, who would surprise the world by summoning a council…
body: Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli, born in 1881 at Sotto il Monte near Bergamo to a family of sharecroppers, had spent decades in the papal diplomatic service, in Bulgaria, in Turkey and Greece, and as nuncio in Paris, before being created cardinal and named Patriarch of Venice in 1953. When Pius XII died on 9 October 1958, Roncalli entered the conclave with a return ticket in his pocket.

On 28 October 1958, the fourth day of the conclave, he was elected on the eleventh ballot and took the name John XXIII, keeping his episcopal motto, Obedientia et pax. Nearly seventy-seven years old, he was widely expected to be a brief, transitional pope.

Within three months, on 25 January 1959, he astonished the Church by announcing an ecumenical council, the first in nearly ninety years. That assembly, the Second Vatican Council, opened in 1962 and reshaped Catholic life for generations. Beloved as "Good Pope John," he died on 3 June 1963 and was canonized in 2014.
